contentSections: Start with a Clear Picture of the Project

Before contacting any facade company, it helps to have basic clarity on the project itself, since this shapes which companies are even worth shortlisting. A homeowner adding a single accent panel to an existing house has very different needs from a business fitting out a new corporate office facade, and approaching both types of company with a vague brief usually produces vague, hard-to-compare quotes. At minimum, it is worth knowing the approximate facade area involved, whether this is new construction or a renovation, a rough budget range, and a general sense of the desired look, even if that is just two or three reference images rather than a finished design.
Step 1: Build a Shortlist

Start by identifying three to five facade companies that have genuine experience with projects similar in scale and type to yours, whether that is residential homes, office buildings, retail spaces or institutional structures. A general online search combined with checking a company's own project portfolio is a reasonable starting point, but it is worth going one step further and looking specifically for projects that are several years old rather than only recent installations, since this reveals how the company's work actually holds up over time rather than how it looks on installation day.
Step 2: Check Track Record and In-House Capability

Once you have a shortlist, dig into how each company actually operates rather than just how their marketing presents them. A company that designs, engineers and fabricates panels in-house is generally more accountable and consistent than one that outsources fabrication to a third party, since there are fewer parties involved if quality issues arise later. Ask how many total projects the company has completed, and if possible, how many of those are comparable in scale to your own project, since a company experienced primarily in small residential accents may not be the right fit for a large commercial facade, and vice versa.
Step 3: Request Detailed, Comparable Quotes

• Give every shortlisted company the same brief, area measurements and reference images, so their quotes are responding to the same scope.
  • Ask for a breakdown of material, fabrication and installation costs rather than a single combined number.
  • Confirm the exact material, thickness and coating type included in the quote, since these details drive most of the price difference between companies.
  • Ask whether waterproofing and substructure work is included or billed separately.
  • Request the proposed project timeline in writing, from design finalisation through to installation completion.
Step 4: Verify Coating and Warranty Terms

The single most important technical detail to confirm before choosing a facade company is the coating specification and its written warranty period, since this determines how the facade will actually look in five, ten and twenty years, far more than the pattern or colour chosen at the outset. PVDF coatings from established manufacturers commonly carry warranties in the range of 15 to 30 years against fading and chalking, while lower grade powder coatings may only be rated for a fraction of that period. Ask specifically what the warranty covers, colour retention, coating integrity, or both, and whether it is backed by the coating manufacturer, the facade company, or both, since this affects what recourse is available if a problem arises after installation.
Step 5: Visit an Experience Centre or Completed Project

Wherever possible, see the material in person before finalising a decision, either at a company's experience centre or showroom, or by visiting a completed project with the company's permission. Photographs and renders, however polished, cannot fully convey how a metal panel catches light, how a colour reads under direct sun compared to indoor lighting, or how a texture feels at close range. This step is particularly important for larger projects or full facade treatments, where a material choice that looks slightly different than expected across an entire building is a far more consequential mistake than the same gap on a small accent panel.
Step 6: Clarify the Contract and After-Sales Terms

Before signing, make sure the contract explicitly states the material specification, coating type and warranty terms, not just the total price and payment schedule, since verbal assurances given during sales conversations do not carry weight if they are not reflected in the written agreement. It is also worth clarifying what happens if a panel is damaged after installation, whether due to an accident, extreme weather or a manufacturing defect that only becomes apparent later. A company confident in its own work should be able to explain a clear process for individual panel replacement without hesitation, since a well-engineered system is generally designed to allow this without disturbing the surrounding facade.

Payment schedules for facade projects typically follow project milestones, such as an advance on order confirmation, a payment on fabrication completion, and a final payment on installation completion, rather than a single upfront lump sum. Being cautious of any company requesting the full payment before fabrication even begins is a reasonable and common-sense precaution.
Timeline Expectations from First Meeting to Installation

Understanding a realistic project timeline helps set expectations and spot companies that are either overpromising or underprepared. The initial consultation and brief development typically takes one to two weeks. Design concept and material selection, including any sampling or mockups, generally takes another two to four weeks depending on project complexity. Detailed engineering and fabrication can range from three to eight weeks depending on the system and whether it is a standard product line or a fully custom parametric design. Installation itself is usually the shortest phase for small to medium projects, often completed within one to three weeks, though larger commercial facades naturally take longer given the volume of panels and coordination involved with other ongoing construction work on site.
For Homeowners: What to Prioritise

Homeowners generally benefit most from prioritising design flexibility and a company's ability to work at a smaller scale, since many residential facade projects involve an accent wall, balcony front or entrance feature rather than a full building treatment. It is worth confirming that a company is genuinely willing to take on a smaller project with the same engineering rigour as a larger one, since some facade companies focus primarily on large commercial contracts and treat residential accents as a lower priority, which can show up in slower response times or less design attention.
For Businesses: What to Prioritise

Business owners and facility managers evaluating a facade company for an office or commercial space should prioritise the company's experience with fire rating compliance, structural load requirements and project timeline reliability, since commercial facades are often tied to a broader construction or fit-out schedule where delays carry real financial cost. It is also worth asking about a company's experience with branding-led design, where the facade needs to reinforce a specific corporate identity or stand out in a commercial corridor, a use case covered in more depth in our guide to commercial elevation design and why it matters for business.
Mistakes to Avoid When Choosing a Facade Company

• Choosing based on price alone without confirming that competing quotes specify the same material grade, thickness and coating.
  • Skipping a site visit or physical sample review and relying only on digital renders before making a final decision.
  • Not asking who is responsible for waterproofing, assuming it is automatically included when it may be billed separately.
  • Finalising a facade company only after construction is already complete, which limits design options and can complicate substructure planning.
  • Overlooking after-sales support and panel replacement policy, which only becomes relevant, and important, years after installation.
Frequently Asked Questions

How many quotes should I get before choosing a facade company?
Three to five detailed quotes from companies with relevant experience is generally enough to compare pricing and approach without the process becoming unmanageable.

What is a reasonable timeline for a facade project in India?
A small residential accent can often be designed and installed within four to eight weeks, while a larger commercial facade may take several months from design finalisation through to completed installation, depending on complexity and project scale.

Is it worth paying more for an established facade company over a local fabricator?
For anything beyond very small or temporary applications, an established company with in-house engineering, a written warranty and a verifiable track record typically reduces long-term risk enough to justify a higher upfront cost.
